---
title: "Cladistic analysis of Maya king lists"
format: html
---

```{r dependencies}
library(cultevo)
library(dplyr)
library(readxl)
library(purrr)
library(tibble)
library(tidyr)
```

```{r data-king-lists}
king_lists <- read_xlsx("data/king-lists.xlsx", col_types = "text") |>
  select(-c(archetype, ...16)) |>
  pivot_longer(!c(Ruler, variants), names_to = "specimen") |>
  mutate(
    value = replace_na(value, "―"), # character absent
    value = na_if(value, "#"),# 
    value = na_if(value, "?") # lemmas
  ) |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = specimen, names_from = c(Ruler, variants)) |> 
  mutate(across(-specimen, as.factor))
```

Hierarchical clustering, based only on the dissimilarity between specimens.

```{r hclust}
king_lists_dist <- hammingdists(column_to_rownames(king_lists, "specimen"))
king_lists_hclust <- hclust(king_lists_dist)
```

```{r fig-hclust}
plot(king_lists_hclust, labels = king_lists$specimen)
```

A phylogenetic tree, which assumes dissimilarities between specimens arose through a process of copying with error (either from each other or from the original).

```{r phylo}
king_lists_phydata <- phyDat(
  sapply(king_lists[,-1], as.numeric),
  type = "USER",
  levels = 0:max(sapply(king_lists[,-1], as.numeric))
)
```
